title: Where to drop a ball intentionally deflected by a person
question: If your ball in motion is intentionally stopped or deflected by a person (not on the green), where should you drop it?

choices.text: Within 1 club-length of where it would have come to rest
At the point where it was struck

explanation: If your ball is intentionally stopped or deflected by a person (not on the green), you must drop a ball within 1 club-length of the estimated spot where it would have come to rest.
imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer, right-handed, standing on a sunny fairway beside a single golf ball, mid-drop, after it was intentionally deflected by a person off the green.
imageAlt: A teen boy golfer on the fairway preparing to drop a ball after it was intentionally stopped by a person.

issues: The golfer's stance and club grip are right-handed, not left-handed as specified in the sceneSpec and final correction.
The dropping hand is the left hand, but for a correct left-handed dropping posture, it should be the right hand.

Clothing colour and hat are accurate, single golf ball is shown, and the iron club is correct.
